extracted.intended_audience: college seniors and recent college graduates applying for the Damon Runyon SPARK post-baccalaureate award; also host institutions and mentors administering the award
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for the Damon Runyon Scholars Program for Advancing Research and Knowledge (SPARK), a one-year post‑baccalaureate research internship for college seniors/recent graduates matched with Damon Runyon scientists. Covers eligibility, selection criteria, funding terms, reporting, and award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion for Research and Pursuit of Knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are evaluated based on their demonstrated commitment to a future in research and thirst for knowledge. Special attention is paid to the personal and career statements submitted as part of the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal and career statements should reflect a deep passion for exploring new horizons in research and a clear articulation of how SPARK aligns with the applicant’s short- and long-term educational and professional goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong academic performance is a fundamental aspect of research and is a primary evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who faced challenging situations that negatively impacted academic performance may explain these challenges in the personal statement; reviewers should consider context provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Recommendation Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of recommendation provides insights into an applicant's character, work ethic, and potential as a future researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should be from individuals who can speak to academic achievements, research aptitude, interpersonal skills, and commitment to professional growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Enrollment / Graduation Timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is open to current college seniors and those who have graduated with a bachelor’s degree within the last 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet this timeframe to be eligible; the program targets recent post-baccalaureate trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Citizenship / Work Authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be U.S. citizens, permanent legal residents, or DACA recipients who are eligible to legally work in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of status/work eligibility will be required; non-eligible applicants should not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Commitment to Future Research and Degree Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be strongly committed to a future career in research and planning to pursue a PhD, MD, DO, or MD/PhD degree following completion of post-baccalaureate research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commitment should be clearly articulated in personal/career statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement for Applicants with Limited Research Access / Underrepresented Backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon encourages applications from seniors and recent graduates who have had limited opportunities to participate in research and from backgrounds typically underrepresented in the sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants coming from economically disadvantaged backgrounds or who experienced challenges reaching their educational goals are strongly encouraged to apply; reviewers should weigh demonstrated opportunity-limitation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match with Damon Runyon Scientist and Host Lab Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SPARK Scholar will be matched with a current or former Damon Runyon scientist at a partnering academic institution and embedded into the host labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholars will have access to all benefits afforded to post-baccalaureate researchers at that institution; host institutions must provide the typical post-bacc support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Participation — Damon Runyon Fellows’ Retreat Attendance and Poster Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars will attend and participate in the 3-day Retreat and each Scholar will present a poster at the retreat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Retreat is a required component to foster networking with Fellows and mentors; presentation quality and participation likely factor into program engagement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Participation — Virtual Quarterly Scientific Communication Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars will participate in virtual quarterly sessions led by Damon Runyon scientists on topics such as manuscript writing, grant writing, and professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance and engagement in these training sessions are part of the program experience and expected to support Scholars' development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-Time Research Requirement and Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon SPARK awards are intended for full-time research. SPARK Scholars are not permitted to hold another position or pursue additional degrees during the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions and applicants should ensure the Scholar can commit full time; concurrent employment or enrollment in other degree programs is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality Agreement Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars may not enter into confidentiality agreements that prevent or delay them from publishing and/or presenting their Damon Runyon-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agreements that would impede dissemination are prohibited; Scholars and mentors must clear potential restrictions before accepting the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Amounts and Award Payment Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual stipend: Up to $50,000; Annual living allowance: Up to $8,500; Travel to meetings and Retreat: Up to $2,500; Total: $61,000. Awards (Stipend/Travel allowance) are made to the host institution in support of the designated Scholar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total stipend should not exceed the level of support for other individuals at the same level of training at that institution. If the full $50,000 is not to be expended as salary, the balance may be applied to Fringe Benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Indirect Costs / Institutional Overhead
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of this award can be used for indirect costs or institutional overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions must budget award funds only for allowable direct costs as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax Guidance and No Employer-Employee Relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars should consult the institution about tax liability. An award/living allowance does not constitute an employer-employee relationship between Damon Runyon and the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions and awardees are responsible for handling tax implications and employment status; Damon Runyon will forward qualified living allowance directly to the Scholar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Reporting Requirements (final progress report)
rubrics_metrics.description: At completion of SPARK, the Scholar must submit a detailed progress report that includes the following items (must be signed by Scholar and Mentor; report not to exceed three pages): a technical summary/evaluation of research performed; two abstracts (one lay, one scientific); bibliography of publications (pdfs if applicable); list of conferences/seminars attended and presentations given; description of collaborations/partnerships with identified affiliations; description of participation in community-based educational mentorship/STEM outreach; statement indicating how SPARK made a difference; statement of future plans; up-to-date CV; and a brief letter from the Mentor assessing the Scholar’s scientific progress and professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should be technical but targeted to a general scientific audience and sufficiently detailed to articulate research activities; figures and references may be included if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Reporting Requirements and Account Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's financial officer must maintain a separate account including receipts for each award, available for audit by Foundation representatives. Upon termination or expiration of the award, a final report of expenditures with refund of any unexpended balance must be submitted within 60 days. Pre-award spending is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Damon Runyon SPARK Scholar Financial Expenditure Report form. Travel expense reporting must include name/location of meeting, dates, and use of funds; travel funds restricted to registration fee, lodging, meals, transportation (if by train or plane, coach class only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications, Presentations, and Website Acknowledgment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications (including abstracts of presentations) resulting from projects supported by Damon Runyon must carry the acknowledgment: "[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon SPARK Scholar supported by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (SPK-# [___])." Awardees should identify themselves as Damon Runyon SPARK Scholars when presenting or on websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact awards@damonrunyon.org if you do not know your SPK #. Download and use the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation logo for PowerPoint, posters, and websites where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Administration — Payment to Host Institution and Program Director Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards (Stipend/Travel allowance) are made to the host institution in support of the designated Scholar. An additional allowance of $1,500 will be given to the Institutional program director of post-baccalaureate training for community building events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions should treat awards as institutional grants (not personnel employer relationships) and allocate the $1,500 for community-building as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Process and Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, log into Altum | Proposal Central and search for Damon Runyon Scholars Program for Advancing Research and Knowledge (SPARK). Applications are due by 4:00 pm Eastern Time on February 2, 2026. Application instructions are located on the Damon Runyon Applications Guidelines webpage and all application forms are located within Proposal Central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to join the SPARK Informational Session (date/time provided) for program and application guidance; ensure forms and materials are submitted through Proposal Central by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and Review Process and Unconscious Bias Reminder
rubrics_metrics.description: The Damon Runyon SPARK Committee will review applications and select awardees for approval by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation’s Board of Directors. Reviewers are reminded of the Foundation’s commitment to excellence and values of diversity, equity, and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the start of review sessions the following is read aloud to reviewers: acknowledgment that unconscious biases exist and that reviewers should be aware of potential biases when reviewing, scoring and discussing candidates and applications.
